name: Oxidus
english_description: A genuinely modern, actively-developed, from-scratch FluffOS mudlib (a distant, long-since-diverged fork of LPUniversity), not a legacy archive -- self-hosts its own real unit test suite, documentation site, and agent-coding guides. Account-based login (register an account, then create/select a character; the first character ever created becomes the mud's owner/admin). Real bespoke content: the village of Olum (square, bakery, tailor, financier, a manor interior with an arcanist NPC/spell tree) plus forest/cavern/maze/tunnels/wastes zones. Assumed a considerably newer/differently-configured driver build than this corpus's shared one in three independent ways, all diagnosed and fixed: native async/await support (the shared build predated fluffos's own async/await merge by days -- fixed with a driver rebuild, not an oxidus-specific change), a bundled include/driver/*.h headers directory the lib's own build pipeline normally generates (copied in by hand), and a hard split between the classic ed() efun this corpus's shared driver is built with (OLD_ED, needed by 800+ other files' own wizard editors) versus the modern ed_start()/ed_cmd()/query_ed_mode() trio this lib's editor module had been rewritten to use, which broke std/living/body.lpc's entire player/NPC inheritance chain at compile time (fixed by reverting to the classic API; new AGENTS.md #7.161). Also fixed: a `private`-declared ed() write/exit callback that function_exists() (and the driver's generic by-name apply()) treats as not-defined for any caller outside the object, so the callback silently never fired with zero error signal anywhere (new AGENTS.md #7.162); a redundant second restore_body() call in login.lpc that silently reverted a promoted admin/dev's role-based command search paths back to their pre-promotion save state on every reconnect, so every /cmds/adm//dev//file command including the in-game editor looked like it didn't exist (new AGENTS.md #8.21); a no-argument adminp()/devp() call in std_setup() checking the wrong identity's privileges; and an unconfigured optional GITHUB_REPORTER integration whose setup-time validation threw instead of degrading gracefully, taking the whole bug/idea/todo commands down instead of just their optional GitHub-filing half. Full registration-to-gameplay playthrough (two independent accounts, reconnect/restore path, in-game ed editor end-to-end including a real permission-gate check) verified live and repeatedly. See libs/oxidus/NOTES.md for the full writeup.
